bib.title: RAFT: Adapting Language Model to Domain Specific RAG

question: How do we adapt pre-trained LLMs for Retrieval Augmented Generation in specialized domains?
hypothesis: Fine-tuning with a mix of golden and distractor documents plus chain-of-thought answers that quote the source teaches the model to read in-domain context and ignore distractors, beating plain domain fine-tuning and RAG-only prompting.
contributions: RAFT training recipe: question + golden doc + distractors, with CoT answers citing verbatim quotes
Ablations on CoT, fraction P of examples with golden doc, and number of train/test distractors

method.summary: Fine-tune LLaMA2-7B-chat on questions paired with one golden document and four distractors for P fraction of examples (distractors only for the rest), with chain-of-thought answers generated by GPT-4-1106 that quote the golden document. Test with top-k retrieved documents in the standard RAG setting and compare to base, RAG and domain-specific fine-tuning baselines.

datasets.name: PubMedQA
datasets.source: Jin et al. 2019 (Dernoncourt & Lee 2017 also cited)

datasets.name: HotpotQA
datasets.preprocessing: golden document may be more than one document; CoT answers generated

datasets.name: HuggingFace Hub / Torch Hub / TensorFlow Hub (Gorilla APIBench)
Natural Questions, TriviaQA
datasets.preprocessing: used in Fig 5 and Fig 6 only

models.name: RAFT (LLaMA2-7B)
models.init_from: inferred: LLaMA2-7B-chat from the baseline description

training.objective: standard supervised fine-tuning to generate CoT answer (reason with ##begin_quote## ##end_quote## citations, then ##Answer) from question + documents

other.P: fraction of examples keeping golden doc; Sec 4.4 text says P=80% helps; optimal 40%, 60% or 100% by dataset; P used for Table 1 not stated

inference.prompting: Baselines: LLaMA2-7B-chat 0-shot with instructions; with RAG reference documents appended; DSF 0-shot; DSF + RAG. Retriever-independent.
inference.retrieval: Table 1 test format: golden document with four distractors (Sec 4.4); Fig 6 uses top-3 retrieved docs, varying top-k 2 to 10. Retriever not named.

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: not defined in text; axes say Final Accuracy

eval.protocol: single numbers in tables, no seeds, no variance, no significance test stated

prompts.purpose: Generate CoT reasoning for training answers
prompts.text: Instruction: Given the question, context and answer above, provide a logical reasoning for that answer. Please use the format of: ##Reason: {reason} ##Answer: {answer}.

evidence.quote: we include four distractor documents alongside the golden document, and at test time, we maintain this format by providing the golden document with four distractors.

results.claim: RAFT beats DSF + RAG on HotpotQA by a wide margin
results.setup: LLaMA2-7B-chat base fine-tuned with RAFT (1 golden + 4 distractor docs, CoT answers with quotes); test with RAG; metric not named in text (figures say Final Accuracy); no seeds or variance reported.
results.table: Table 1, row RAFT (LLaMA2-7B), column HotPot (35.28) vs row DSF + RAG (4.41)

results.claim: RAFT improves HuggingFace over DSF + RAG
results.setup: LLaMA2-7B-chat base fine-tuned with RAFT (1 golden + 4 distractor docs, CoT answers with quotes); test with RAG; metric not named in text (figures say Final Accuracy); no seeds or variance reported.
results.table: Table 1, row RAFT (LLaMA2-7B), column HuggingFace (74.00) vs row DSF + RAG (42.59)

results.claim: RAFT on PubMed vs DSF + RAG (binary yes/no, small gain)
results.setup: LLaMA2-7B-chat base fine-tuned with RAFT (1 golden + 4 distractor docs, CoT answers with quotes); test with RAG; metric not named in text (figures say Final Accuracy); no seeds or variance reported.
results.note: Authors: no significant gain on PubMed since binary yes/no.
results.table: Table 1, row RAFT (LLaMA2-7B), column PubMed (73.30) vs row DSF + RAG (71.6)

results.claim: On Torch Hub and TensorFlow, RAFT is essentially tied with DSF (no RAG)
results.setup: LLaMA2-7B-chat base fine-tuned with RAFT (1 golden + 4 distractor docs, CoT answers with quotes); test with RAG; metric not named in text (figures say Final Accuracy); no seeds or variance reported.
results.note: Margins 0.01 (Torch Hub) and 0.30 (TensorFlow); text says 'consistently and significantly outperforms' without significance test.
results.table: Table 1, row RAFT (LLaMA2-7B), columns Torch Hub (84.95), TensorFlow (86.86) vs row DSF (84.94, 86.56)

results.claim: GPT-3.5 + RAG beats RAFT on HotpotQA (41.5 vs 35.28), though the text says RAFT shows significant advantages over GPT-3.5
results.setup: LLaMA2-7B-chat base fine-tuned with RAFT (1 golden + 4 distractor docs, CoT answers with quotes); test with RAG; metric not named in text (figures say Final Accuracy); no seeds or variance reported.
results.note: Contradiction between table and Sec 4.1 prose.
results.table: Table 1, row GPT-3.5 + RAG, column HotPot (41.5)

results.claim: Adding RAG to a domain-finetuned model does not reliably help; authors attribute this to no training on context
results.setup: DSF vs DSF + RAG, Table 1: HotPot 6.38 to 4.41, HuggingFace 61.06 to 42.59, Torch Hub 84.94 to 82.80, TensorFlow 86.56 to 60.29, PubMed 59.7 to 71.6.
results.quote: introducing RAG to a domain-specifically fine-tuned (DSF) model doesn’t invariably lead to better outcomes.

results.claim: Stated gain over base Llama-2 on HotpotQA
results.note: Matches 35.28-0.03 and 84.95-8.60: absolute points, not relative.
results.quote: The gain can be as big as 35.25% on Hotpot QA and 76.35% on Torch Hub evaluation.

results.claim: Stated gain over DSF on HuggingFace
results.setup: RAFT vs DSF + RAG per arithmetic on Table 1 (35.28-4.41, 74.00-42.59), though the text says compared with DSF.
results.note: Text says DSF; arithmetic matches DSF + RAG.

results.claim: Chain-of-thought answers improve HotpotQA in the ablation
results.setup: RAFT vs RAFT without CoT, Table 2 (HotpotQA 35.28 vs 25.62; HuggingFace 74.00 vs 59.07).
results.note: CoT does not help everywhere: Torch Hub 86.56 (w.o. CoT) vs 84.95 (RAFT).
results.quote: With a gains of 9.66% and 14.93% in the Hotpot QA and HuggingFace datasets respectively.

results.claim: Including some training examples without the golden document helps in-domain RAG
results.setup: NQ, TriviaQA, HotpotQA; Fig 5 (values only plotted, not tabulated).
results.note: Inconsistent: Sec 4.4 text says P=80% but then says optimal P varies across datasets as 40%, 60% and 100%.
results.quote: incorporating a portion of the training data without the golden document in the context (P = 80%) appears to enhance the model’s performance on RAG tasks.

results.claim: Training with distractor docs makes the model robust to the number of test-time documents; golden-only training is poor
results.setup: Fig 6, test with top-3 docs / varying top-k from 2 to 10; Llama-2-7B variants.
results.note: Text says D*+3D best for NQ and D*+1D for HotpotQA, inconsistent with caption; paper then fixes 1 golden + 4 distractors.
results.quote: we find that training with 4 documents leads to optimal performance, and this changes to 3 and 2 for for Trivia QA and HotPot QA respectively.

results.claim: Qualitative case: DSF answers with a film name where RAFT gives the screenwriter

limits: No hyperparameters, dataset sizes, hardware or seeds are given; no appendix.
Setting is the same documents at train and test (in-domain); the authors say other fine-tuning-for-RAG works test on different domains.
Metric is never defined; no variance or significance tests.
Internal inconsistencies: P=80% vs 40/60/100%; best distractor count in text vs Fig 6 caption; GPT-3.5 beats RAFT on HotpotQA yet text claims advantage.
Fig 3 caption describes a self-critique prompt but the figure shows CoT generation.
Torch Hub, TensorFlow, PubMed gains over DSF are tiny or none; PubMed is binary yes/no.
